scenes.title: dbt Project Structure & Setup
scenes.narration: This lesson walks through how a dbt project is organized on disk and how dbt learns to connect to your warehouse.

scenes.title: The key project files
bullets: dbt_project.yml declares the project and its defaults
The models/ directory holds your SQL transformations
scenes.narration: Every dbt project centers on a file called dbt_project.yml, which names the project and sets default behaviors such as materializations. Your transformation logic lives in the models directory as SQL files. Connection details like host, user, and warehouse live separately in profiles.yml, which keeps credentials out of your version-controlled code.

scenes.title: A minimal dbt_project.yml
scenes.code:
name: 'analytics'
profile: 'analytics'
version: '1.0.0'

models:
  analytics:
    staging:
      +materialized: view
    marts:
      +materialized: table
scenes.narration: Here is a minimal project configuration. The name identifies the project and the profile line tells dbt which connection block in profiles.yml to use. Under the models key we configure defaults per folder, so everything in staging is built as a lightweight view while everything in marts is built as a persisted table. Configuring materializations by folder like this saves you from repeating settings in every single model.

scenes.title: The staging-to-marts layering
steps: staging: clean and rename raw columns
scenes.narration: A conventional dbt project flows through layered folders. Staging models clean and rename raw source columns one-to-one, intermediate models handle heavier joins and reshaping, and marts expose the final business-ready tables that stakeholders query. This layering keeps each model small, focused, and easy to reason about.

scenes.text: Run dbt debug after setup to confirm your profile connects to the warehouse before you build anything.
scenes.narration: Before building models, always run dbt debug, which verifies that your profile is found and that dbt can actually reach the warehouse, saving you from chasing confusing errors later.
